title: A Readout-Aware Theory of Approximate Heisenberg Propagation
authors: Yubraj Bhandari, Jakob S. Kottmann, Adelina Bärligea
abstract: Classical methods for computing quantum expectation values often propagate observables in the Heisenberg picture. To remain tractable, these methods rely on approximations that discard operator components during evolution. Yet the magnitude of these components alone does not determine the resulting expectation-value error, which also depends on their subsequent evolution and the input state. We develop \emph{generalized Pauli propagation}, a common algebraic framework encompassing Pauli propagation, Lie-algebraic simulation, and Krylov subspace methods. Using weighted commutator graphs, we derive exact identities that relate approximation errors to the signed contributions of omitted and discarded operator components. Our central result establishes \emph{delayed observability}, identifying conditions under which these contributions vanish at low orders in propagation time. We use this structure to develop finite-order error estimates and state-dependent selection rules. We further prove that retaining the symmetry-preserving part of a weak perturbation eliminates first-order expectation-value errors under suitable symmetry conditions. By revealing how approximation errors affect the desired expectation value, our framework provides a basis for more informative error analysis and the development of readout-aware simulation strategies.
summary: This paper introduces a generalized Pauli propagation framework to rigorously analyze errors in computing quantum expectation values. By mapping dynamics onto a weighted commutator graph, the authors derive exact identities quantifying how approximation errors accumulate. This provides a powerful, readout-aware tool for developing more accurate and reliable quantum simulation strategies.
main_problem: The paper addresses the challenge of efficiently and accurately computing quantum expectation values $\langle O(t) angle$ in the Heisenberg picture, where approximations often discard crucial operator components.
main_result: The authors develop a framework establishing 'delayed observability,' providing exact identities to quantify approximation errors based on signed contributions of omitted components, leading to state-dependent error estimates.
method: The core method is 'generalized Pauli propagation,' which maps the evolution onto a weighted commutator graph and reduces the problem to a bilinear exponential action on a finite-dimensional subspace.
model_or_system: The theory applies to general quantum many-body dynamics governed by Hamiltonians, using the adjoint action $	ext{ad}_H$ to track the evolution of observables $O$. Specific tests involve Ising and circuit ensembles.
key_observables: Expectation value $\langle O(t) angle$, approximation error ($\epsilon_{	ext{mv}}(t)$), and the weighted commutator graph structure.
important_parameters: Propagation time ($t$), perturbation strength ($\epsilon$), and the order of approximation ($p$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on restricting the dynamics to a finite-dimensional invariant subspace $V$ and deriving error bounds based on graph structure, though cancellations can invalidate simple bounds.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the unified graph picture of the mean value calculation, showing the source-to-readout transfer, and comparing relative estimation errors and sign accuracy for different circuit depths.
paper_structure: The paper builds from defining the general problem via the commutator graph, deriving exact error identities (delayed observability), and then applying this framework to test its efficacy across various physical models and approximation schemes.
why_interesting: This work provides a rigorous, graph-theoretic framework for error analysis in quantum simulation, which is crucial for developing reliable numerical techniques for open quantum systems and dynamics.
